description: customManagers:githubActionsVersions and customManagers:dockerfileVersions pick up `# renovate: datasource=... depName=...` above a *_VERSION env in a workflow, or above an ARG/ENV *_VERSION in a Dockerfile; the first custom manager below reads the same marker in .tf, .env, .sh and other YAML files. The built-in managers only read uses:, container images, runs-on and FROM, so without them those markers are inert and every pinned CLI in the fleet is frozen until someone edits it by hand.

customManagers.description: The `# renovate:` marker grammar of customManagers:dockerfileVersions, for pins no other manager reads: the next line holds the value as KEY=value (.env, .sh), default = "value" (.tf) or a lowercase key: value (YAML). The lowercase key keeps it clear of githubActionsVersions, which owns the uppercase *_VERSION: lines in workflows, so no marker is read twice

Go analysis tool pins that the reusables on both forges expose as workflow_call input defaults (`<tool>_version:` ... `default: 'vX.Y.Z'`). No other manager reads an input default, so these froze until the go lane moved to a Go release the old golangci-lint and staticcheck could not parse
Python tool pins that the python-cicd reusables on both forges expose as input defaults, same shape as the Go tools above. python_image is the Forgejo job container

ARG GO_VERSION feeding FROM golang:${GO_VERSION}-alpine. The dockerfile manager resolves the base image digest but never the interpolated Go version, so each repo's toolchain stayed put until a stale Go stdlib failed the Grype release gate

Same ARG in its floating major.minor form (golang:1.26-alpine keeps taking patch releases). golang-version only knows full versions, so the golang image tags are the lookup, which keeps the value floating
Swift packages declared in an XcodeGen project.yml. The swift manager only reads Package.swift, and the generated xcodeproj with its Package.resolved is gitignored, so nothing else reads these pins

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Raise a PR the moment osv.dev reports a CVE in something we depend on, instead of waiting for the CI that scans for it to go red. osvVulnerabilityAlerts is the half that works on both forges: GitHub's own alert feed needs the Dependabot API, which Forgejo does not serve, while osv.dev is queried directly and needs no forge support at all. The rules osv.dev produces are appended after everything below and carry a force block, so they reach a dependency an earlier rule disabled - which is the point, since the gomod manager disables indirect requirements by default and a vulnerable indirect is exactly what govulncheck fails a build over. Left ungrouped and out of the daily batch on purpose: a security bump that shares a PR with thirty routine ones cannot be merged any faster than the slowest of them

packageRules.description: Supply-chain cooldown: no update is raised until its version has been public for 7 days, which is the window in which hijacked tags and malicious publishes usually get caught and pulled. Replaces best-practices' 3-day npm-only rule. Security fixes are not delayed: vulnerabilityAlerts defaults to minimumReleaseAge null and the osv.dev rules carry it

Docker updates Renovate cannot date would otherwise be held forever without a word (the dependency dashboard is off) under Renovate 42+'s timestamp-required default: everything on GHCR, which serves no timestamps, and every digest update on a floating tag (latest, alpine, nonroot), which has no release to date. timestamp-optional only drops the requirement: an update that has a timestamp still waits the full cooldown. Accepted gap: undated docker updates land with no wait
Our own modules and images skip the cooldown: we publish them, so there is no third party to wait out, and a 7-day hold on a shared/ digest or a freshly tagged image only delays our own fixes

Automerge safe update types, pre-1.0 minor bumps included, batched into one PR per repo so each run's updates clear in a single green run. Renovate only arms the merge once it sees the branch already green, so rebaseWhen stays off auto: a rebase on every base-branch move restarts CI and burns that run

The Go analysis tool pins above are defaults every caller inherits the moment they merge, so they get their own PR instead of riding the batch. Both reusables repos gate it with a required canary check (canary.yml + scripts/canary.sh) that runs the old and the new version over every caller and goes red when the new one fails where the old one passes. Green means no caller breaks, so it automerges; red waits for a person

ruff decides what clean means for every python caller (its default rule set grows between releases) and no canary covers them, so the python tool pins get their own PR and wait for a person to re-run ruff over the callers. bandit and the job image ride along

Lint and release-note tools the fleet's gates run: zizmor (both reusables repos and forgejo-fleet-ops), hadolint (both reusables repos), git-cliff (release notes on both forges), kube-score (Kubernetes) and tflint (infra-ci). A new release can add rules that turn every caller red at once, or change what the release notes say, so the pins get their own PR and wait for a person
A docker tag captured by a regex manager has no digest group next to it, so a pinDigest update has nowhere to write and only produces an empty branch
Lockfile refreshes stay in their own PR. Grouped with the rest, one unresolvable peer dependency would block every unrelated bump in the batch
Majors stay manual and get the major label. The dependency dashboard is off, so the open PRs are the only list: search both forges for that label

Callers ride the shared workflows at @master (Forgejo: @main) by design; never pin or update those refs. The Forgejo one also has to be here because Renovate reads a .forgejo/workflows `uses:` as a github-actions dep and looks the repo up on github.com, where it does not exist
svelte-check cannot typecheck under TypeScript 7 yet; lift once the Svelte toolchain supports it

aws/aws-sdk-go-v2 carries ~83k git tags. Renovate's github-tags datasource orders refs by TAG_COMMIT_DATE, which now exceeds GitHub's 10s GraphQL budget at every page size, so the changelog lookup 504s and takes the whole run down with it. Version resolution goes through the go datasource and is unaffected; only release-note fetching has to be skipped
